prompt_text: I need my roof replaced in Dallas. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I just need one quick detail: what ZIP code or neighborhood in Dallas is the roof located in? Dallas is big and the best contractors vary by neighborhood and workload.

If you want an immediate plan without giving location, here’s a practical, safe approach and why each type of company is useful. If you prefer, give the ZIP and I’ll produce 3–5 specific, vetted contractors (with phone numbers and reasons) for your address.

Which companies to call (and why)
- A large, national roofer with storm/insurance-claim experience (e.g., Baker Roofing Company or another national firm)
  - Why: They handle big storm seasons, know insurance adjusters, and can manage complex claims and permits. Good if you expect an insurance claim or large replacement.
- A GAF Master Elite or CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster certified local contractor
  - Why: Manufacturer-certified contractors can offer better product warranties and have met training/insurance/quality requirements. Use GAF/CertainTeed “Find a Pro” tools to locate certified installers near you.
- An experienced, long-established Dallas roofer (local family-owned)
  - Why: Local firms have long-standing relationships, quicker response for warranty/service calls, and knowledge of local codes/inspectors.
- A highly rated independent roofer with strong online reviews and BBB accreditation
  - Why: Often competitive pricing and personalized service; check BBB rating, Google reviews, and references.
- A public adjuster (only if you’re filing a complicated insurance claim)
  - Why: They can help maximize your insurance payout and negotiate with the insurance company, though they charge a fee or percentage.

What I’ll check for when vetting specific companies
- Proof of insurance (general liability and workers’ comp)
- Written estimate with material, labor, permit, and disposal line items
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) and warranty details
- Local references (past nearby jobs) and photos
- Local business address, Texas inspections/permits experience
- BBB rating and recent Google/Yelp reviews (look for patterns, not single bad reviews)
- License/registration requirements: Texas has limited statewide licensing for roofers, so check city permits and roofing permit history

Questions to ask when you call (script)
- Are you licensed/insured? Can you email certificates for liability and workers’ comp?
- Are you a certified installer for any manufacturer (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning)? Which?
- Can you provide 3 recent local references and pictures of completed jobs?
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections? Who gets the permit?
- What is included in the written estimate? (materials, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, drip edge, disposal)
- What warranties do you provide (labor + manufacturer)? How long?
- What is the project timeline and start date? When will you be on site each day?
- Who will manage the project onsite and who is the point of contact?

Red flags
- Asks for full payment up front or large cash-only deposits
- No written contract or vague scope of work
- Pushy claims about “storm inspection” or pressuring to sign immediately
- No local address, poor or no references, or unverifiable insurance

Next step
- Tell me your Dallas ZIP code or neighborhood and whether this is an insurance claim. I’ll return a short, specific list of 3–5 contractors in your area with phone numbers, notable credentials, and which one I’d recommend first and why.
